brief.ask: Set the rules for turning Plajah’s ~45 Tela design-history eras (Art Deco, Bauhaus, Constructivism, Memphis, Ukiyo-e principles, Harlem Renaissance editorial, Afrofuturism, Vaporwave and more) into evite versions: built procedurally in code from each era’s palette, type and ornament, so they cost no image credits.
brief.audience: Design-literate hosts and anyone who wants a party with a point of view.
brief.feeling: A museum-grade style lesson you can send.
constraints: Surface: Plajah Evites, an invitation opened on a phone browser by guests who never sign up; also shared as a link preview and QR.

Build method (fixed): each design is a layered Tela document: a generated art plate, separate transparent foreground cut-outs that drift and react to phone tilt, a WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer, light leaks, bokeh, particles, candle flicker) revealed through masks, and live text in Tela. Names, dates and venues are never baked into the art.
Bar: consumer-facing, jaw-dropping, high-end professional. Must stay legible at 390px wide, honour reduced motion, and load fast on mobile data.
No copyrighted characters; kids art is original or Plajah-owned.

Production is GENERATIVE ONLY (Magnific image models, shaders, procedural code, renders of Plajah-owned 3D assets). One Magnific draft grid returns 8 to 16 distinct plates for a flat cost, so a whole collection can be explored in one or two prompts: direct those prompts.

proposals.title: The Canon, Codified
proposals.idea: Every era is rendered as a constitutional document — a single governing proportion system stated before any content exists, from which palette, type scale, ornament grammar, and motion intervals all derive without exception, so the evite does not illustrate a style but enacts it structurally.
proposals.geometry: Each era receives one cantus firmus: a primary measure (column width, circle radius, or diagonal angle) declared in the first render pass and never renegotiated. Art Deco locks a 1:1.618 golden section that governs panel division, chevron repeat, and text-block width simultaneously. Bauhaus locks a 9-unit modular grid at 390px ÷ 9 = 43.3px, every element sitting on or spanning whole units. Constructivism locks a single 35° diagonal that controls all ruled lines, image crops, and foil-vector direction. Memphis locks a 24px dot-grid from which every squiggle, stripe, and color-block originates. Ukiyo-e principles lock a three-plane depth hierarchy (sky field, middle-ground action, foreground fragment) with fixed vertical proportions 60 / 30 / 10. No era shares its measure with another. The grid is not decoration; it is the load-bearing wall.
proposals.typography: Each era draws from a single open-license type pairing that is historically grounded, never approximate. Art Deco: Poiret One (display, tracked +120, all caps) over Josefin Sans (text, tracked +40). Bauhaus: BioRhyme Expanded (bold geometric, caps) over Space Grotesk (body). Constructivism: Bebas Neue (condensed slab, 90° rotated label) over IBM Plex Mono (detail data). Memphis: Righteous (round grotesque, mixed case) over Nunito (body). Ukiyo-e: Shippori Mincho (vertical-capable serif, large) over Noto Serif JP (caption). Harlem Renaissance: Playfair Display (italic headline) over Lora (editorial body, generous leading). Afrofuturism: Orbitron (display) over Exo 2 (body). Vaporwave: VT323 (pixel display) over Share Tech Mono (body). Scale is set by a modular type scale whose ratio matches the era's geometric measure: golden-section eras use 1.618, grid eras use 1.333, diagonal eras use
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs enter. Every art plate is generated by Magnific from era-specific prompt grammars directed by this team: Art Deco receives a prompt for sunburst gouache on black ground, no faces, no text; Constructivism receives a prompt for red-black lithograph geometry with deliberate registration offset; Ukiyo-e receives a prompt for woodblock bokashi gradient sky with wave fragment, flat colour, no photographic depth. One Magnific draft grid of 8–16 plates per era explores the full compositional range at flat cost. The selected plate enters Tela as the locked background layer. Foreground cut-outs are procedurally generated SVG ornaments — chevrons, constructivist bars, Memphis squiggles, mon crests — never photographs, never scans. The image is not illustrative; it is the structural field from which type and ornament are read against.
proposals.texture: Texture is era-faithful and substrate-specific, all simulated via shader or Magnific prompt direction. Art Deco: gold-leaf foil grain, slight emboss shadow on raised panel edges. Bauhaus: uncoated press stock, slight ink squeeze at stroke terminals. Constructivism: newsprint tooth, visible halftone dot at 45° in mid-tones. Memphis: glossy offset, flat and clean — texture is absence of texture, which is itself a material statement. Ukiyo-e: washi paper grain in sky field only, woodblock ink bleed at contour edges. Harlem Renaissance: cream stock, letterpress deboss depth on headline. Afrofuturism: chrome foil substrate, holographic scatter in highlight zone. Vaporwave: CRT phosphor glow, scan-line overlay at 1px interval. Every texture is a WebGL shader parameter, not a bitmap overlay, so it scales without resolution penalty.
proposals.motion: Motion obeys the same hierarchy as space: the governing measure is stated first, all subsequent movement derives from it. Sequence is fixed: (1) background plate fades to full opacity at 0.6 s ease-in — the field is established before anything else exists. (2) Structural ornament (grid lines, diagonals, borders) draws on at 0.8 s over 400 ms — the skeleton arrives before flesh. (3) Foreground cut-outs drift into position at 1.0 s, parallax gain proportional to the era's depth-plane count: Ukiyo-e three planes each at ×0.4 / ×0.7 / ×1.0 tilt-response; flat eras (Bauhaus, Constructivism) receive ×0.0 tilt on background, ×0.6 on foreground only, honouring their anti-illusionist doctrine. (4) WebGL foil or glow layer resolves at 1.4 s. (5) Live text types on at 1.6 s — names and dates arrive last because they are the content the structure was built to carry. Reduced-motion mode: all animatio
proposals.productionMethod: Each era is a Tela document template with four locked layers: (A) generated art plate from Magnific, 390×844px, era-specific prompt grammar, selected from an 8–16 plate draft grid; (B) procedural SVG ornament layer generated by era-specific code rules (chevron generator, grid-line renderer, mon-crest builder) with no manual drawing; (C) WebGL effects layer: foil shimmer keyed to the plate's declared light-source angle, bokeh radius and particle count set by era parameters, candle-flicker enabled only for eras with warm-light grammars; (D) live Tela text layer, typefaces loaded from Google Fonts CDN, fields for name / date / venue / host never baked. The prompt grammar for each era is a documented specification — not a casual description — naming colour space (Munsell references where attributable), compositional rule, forbidden elements, and required structural feature. One prompt gramma
proposals.humanTrace: The human trace is editorial and directorial, not gestural: the proportion system was chosen by a person who read the history; the prompt grammar was written by a person who knows what a Bauhaus grid actually does versus what a Memphis grid does; the plate was selected from 16 options by a person who can say 'that does not resolve.' The shader parameters were set by a person who decided that Constructivism gets no foil shimmer because shimmer is decorative and Constructivism is anti-decorative. These are not algorithmic defaults; they are argued positions. The human trace is the argument.
proposals.risk: The risk is that structural fidelity produces work that reads as academic — museum-correct but cold, a style lesson without seduction. That risk is worth taking because the brief explicitly calls for a museum-grade style lesson, and a lesson that flatters its subject by softening its rules teaches nothing. The answer to coldness is not to loosen the structure but to make the structure itself the dramatic event: when the Constructivist diagonal arrives at 0.8 s and the type snaps to it at 1.6 s, the discipline is the jaw-drop.

arguesWith.why: The Rebellious Hand will argue that locking a cantus firmus before content exists is exactly the kind of a priori hierarchy that kills responsive making — that the era's energy lives in its ruptures and accidents, not its rules, and that my approach produces a pastiche of correctness rather than a living thing. I answer: a rupture is only legible against a rule it breaks. Memphis without its grid

proposals.title: Ink Pressure, Not Pixel Polish
proposals.idea: Each era's evite is built from a procedurally-simulated printmaking process — letterpress, screen-print, risograph, woodblock — so the design history lesson is also a lesson in how that era actually made marks, with registration drift, ink spread, and plate wear baked into the shader logic as evidence, not ornament.
proposals.geometry: No era shares a grid. Constructivism gets a diagonal axis at 22.5° with bleed-to-edge bars. Art Deco gets a strict golden-ratio column with centered symmetry. Memphis gets an intentionally broken 5-column that refuses to resolve. Ukiyo-e gets a vertical scroll proportion (9:19) with negative space weighted to the upper third. Harlem Renaissance editorial gets a two-column broadside with a fat rule interrupting it. The grid IS the argument about the era — not a neutral container.
proposals.typography: Playfair Display (OFL) for Art Deco headers — tracked wide, caps, treated as a block of metal. Space Grotesk (OFL) for Bauhaus — optically sized so the x-height dominates. Libre Baskerville (OFL) for Harlem Renaissance — set in tight justified columns to simulate hot-type pressure. Dela Gothic One (OFL) for Memphis — oversized, color-split with a 2px registration offset on the second layer. Zen Old Mincho (OFL) for Ukiyo-e — vertical-rl text, not simulated, actually set vertical. All event data (name, date, venue) lives in live Tela text, never baked. Type scale is never decorative — point size answers to the era's production constraint: what fit on a press bed, what fit on a zine page.
proposals.imageLogic: The art plate for each era is a Magnific prompt directed at the era's actual production method, not its aesthetic: 'risograph two-color misregistration, cyan and coral, halftone dot visible at 200%, paper tooth showing through ink' or 'woodblock relief print, ink starvation at stroke edges, grain of the block in the negative space.' One Magnific draft grid per era cluster — Art Deco / Bauhaus / Constructivism in one grid pass, Memphis / Vaporwave / Afrofuturism in another — returns 8–16 plates. Editorial selection happens here: I am choosing which plate shows the most honest process evidence, not the prettiest result. Foreground cut-outs are procedurally masked silhouettes that drift on tilt — they are never the hero, they are the thing the print was always reaching toward.
proposals.texture: Shader-simulated ink on paper: Perlin-noise paper tooth at 0.4–1.2px grain, ink spread modeled as a radial blur keyed to stroke width, plate wear as a slow-drift UV offset (0.0003 per frame) that means the design is never identical twice. For risograph eras the two-color layers carry independent registration offsets (±3px X, ±2px Y) declared before generation and locked across the run — this is the registration mark on the press, the physical fact every element answers to. For letterpress eras: deboss simulation via a normal-map displacement shader, depth 0.8–1.4px, light source at the declared polar angle. Texture is process, not finish.
proposals.motion: Entrance: the plate appears as if pulled from a press — a wipe from the gripper edge (top on portrait, left on landscape) at 280ms, ease-out. Ink spread blooms outward from that edge for 120ms after. Foreground cut-outs drift in tilt-response at 6–14px parallax depending on depth plane — slower than The Baroque Dramatist would want, because the motion should feel like paper lifting, not cinema. Registration offset on the two-color layers oscillates ±0.5px at 0.2Hz — imperceptible as animation, perceptible as material instability. Candle-flicker WebGL (Perlin at 0.3–1.8Hz) applies only to eras with candlelit production history — Art Deco, Harlem Renaissance — not universally. Reduced motion: plate appears at full opacity, no wipe, no tilt, registration offset frozen at declared value. Nothing is lost conceptually.
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific draft-grid prompts cover the full 45-era collection in clusters of related production logic. Each prompt specifies: era, simulated print process, declared light azimuth and elevation (locked before writing the prompt), paper stock (newsprint / coated / Japanese washi / blueprint), color count (1 to 4, process-accurate), and one specific imperfection to preserve (ink starvation, halftone moiré, woodgrain bleed). From each grid I select 8 plates editorially. Foreground cut-outs are generated separately as masked elements — clean alpha, tilt-reactive in Tela's parallax layer. WebGL shaders are written procedurally: paper grain, ink spread, registration drift, foil shimmer for eras where foil was a prestige marker (Art Deco, 1980s luxury print). All live text is Tela-native. Zero image credits spent on type or event data.
proposals.humanTrace: The registration offset. Every two-color era carries a declared X/Y misregistration value (e.g., Constructivism: +2px X, -1px Y) chosen before the first prompt is written and locked across the entire run of that era's plates. That prior decision — a number, a commitment, a mistake that is not a mistake — functions like a registration mark on a press. Every shimmer angle, every shadow offset, every bokeh origin answers to it. You can see it. It is not symmetrical. It was not smoothed out. That is the human trace: the decision to be off by exactly this much, on purpose, before the machine was involved.
proposals.risk: The risk is that design-literate hosts will read the misregistration and grain as low-budget rather than intentional — that the process evidence reads as error instead of argument. That risk is worth taking because the alternative is a museum-grade style lesson delivered in a frame so polished it forgets what these eras actually cost to make. A risograph is not a Risograph because it is pretty. It is a Risograph because someone loaded a drum and pulled a print and the second color did not land exactly where the first one did. If we sand that off, we are not teaching design history — we are selling a vibe.

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will strip the registration drift and call it noise. Will say the concept is clear without it — that the era's geometry and type are enough argument. Wrong. Remove the drift and you have a clean evocation of the era's aesthetic. Keep it and you have evidence of its making. Those are not the same thing. The Minimalist edits until nothing can be argued with. I leave the thing in that

proposals.title: The Curtain Rises on History
proposals.idea: Each evite is a theatrical diorama where a single motivated light source — historically calibrated to the era's dominant illumination technology (gaslight, neon, incandescent, candlelight, fluorescent tube) — conducts every shimmer, shadow offset, bokeh origin, and foil angle across all layers simultaneously, so the guest does not read the era, they stand inside it.
proposals.geometry: Portrait stage: a fixed 390×844px proscenium proportioned to a phone screen as a theatre's picture-frame arch. The plate occupies the full bleed; foreground cut-outs are placed on a depth grid of three planes — far, mid, lip — so parallax tilt creates genuine recession, not surface shimmer. The text zone is always the apron: a horizontal band anchored to the bottom third, separated from the image field by a single era-appropriate threshold (a hairline rule in Deco, a Constructivist bar, a Memphis squiggle, a Ukiyo-e cloud band) that functions as a proscenium lip. No centred-on-white cards. The stage is always full.
proposals.typography: Era-matched from OFL only. Art Deco: Cormorant (high-contrast, swashed) at display size with extreme tight tracking, all caps. Bauhaus: BioRhyme or Space Grotesk, geometric, single weight, oversized numerals. Constructivism: Oswald Condensed, forced diagonal baseline via CSS transform, red rule interruption. Memphis: Boogaloo for display, IBM Plex Mono for detail — deliberate clash. Ukiyo-e: Noto Serif JP for Japanese-script guests (collaboration-gated for culturally specific kanji composition), Cormorant Garamond for romanised overlay. Harlem Renaissance editorial: Playfair Display, generous leading, drop-cap scaled to three lines. Afrofuturism: Orbitron display cut against Noto Sans for body — the tension is the message. Vaporwave: VT323 monospace, full-width, scanline CSS overlay. In every era: name, date, venue live in Tela's text layer — never baked — and inherit the era's type rule
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs enter. Every plate is a Magnific generative render directed as an era-faithful environment: not an illustration of the era but a spatial scene lit by the era's light source. Art Deco prompt directs a gilded interior with a single overhead pendant casting 15° shadow at lower-left; Bauhaus directs a white workshop under a north-facing skylight, cool diffuse, no shadow drama; Constructivism directs a factory floor under a single high window, harsh raking light at 35° right; Ukiyo-e directs a flat-perspective scene with no cast shadow but atmospheric gradation — the light source is the sky itself, direction dissolved. One Magnific draft grid of 8–16 plates explores the full collection in one or two prompts. Each plate is then separated: background (full bleed, static), two to three foreground cut-out elements (generative masks applied in Tela, transparent PNGs, assigned to dep
proposals.texture: Materially specific to the era and simulated in shaders, never photoscanned. Deco: embossed gold foil on deep lacquer, simulated with a specular highlight shader that rolls with tilt. Bauhaus: uncoated matte stock, no gloss, slight paper tooth via a noise overlay at 4% opacity. Constructivism: letterpress ink crush on rough newsprint — ink-bleed shader at edges, halftone dot pattern in background fills. Memphis: glossy laminate, flat colour with hard vector ornaments procedurally drawn in code (no image credits consumed). Ukiyo-e: washi paper grain shader, woodblock registration-slip effect (a 2px colour ghost offset on foreground elements). Harlem Renaissance: warm cream stock, slight foxing texture at 3% opacity, deep ink. Afrofuturism: holographic substrate — the foil shimmer shader runs across the entire plate, not just type. Vaporwave: CRT phosphor glow shader, scanline CSS, chromat
proposals.motion: Three-act timing in every evite. Act One (load, 0–800ms): the background plate fades in from black — not a dissolve, a curtain lift: opacity climbs with a cubic-bezier that accelerates mid-fade, mimicking a theatre batten rising. Act Two (settle, 800ms–2s): foreground cut-outs drift in from their depth planes, each on a staggered delay (far plane first, lip last), using a spring easing that overshoots 4px and settles — the tactile weight of a physical object finding rest. The light-source shader activates at 1.2s and propagates its angle across foil, bokeh, and shadow simultaneously — not sequentially. Act Three (live, 2s onward): continuous candle-flicker or neon-pulse or fluorescent-stutter shader runs at the era's historically accurate frequency (candle: 0.3–1.8 Hz; neon: 0.5–2 Hz; fluorescent: 50/60 Hz rendered as a 2% opacity pulse so it reads as ambience, not seizure risk). proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific prompt grid per era cluster (Deco/Bauhaus/Constructivism as one grid; Memphis/Vaporwave/Afrofuturism as one; Ukiyo-e/Harlem as one with collaboration gate noted) returns 8–16 plates. Editorial selection in Tela: choose two to three plates per era as the canonical set. Masks for foreground cut-outs are generated in the same Magnific pass using subject-isolation prompting. WebGL shaders (foil, bokeh, candle-flicker, neon, scanline, paper-tooth noise) are written once as a shader library with era-specific parameter presets — light angle, frequency, specular intensity, grain opacity — swapped via a JSON config file per era. CSS type classes are one file with era-keyed overrides. The proscenium-lip threshold element (hairline, bar, squiggle, cloud band) is drawn in procedural SVG per era — no image credits. Total image credit cost: three Magnific grid runs for ~45 eras. Everythin
proposals.humanTrace: The light source. Every era's dominant illumination technology is researched, named, and its physical behaviour (direction, colour temperature, falloff curve, flicker frequency) is encoded as the single parameter that conducts the entire composition. This is not a filter applied after the fact; it is the first decision made before any prompt is written. The guest feels it as atmosphere — warmth, unease, glamour, clinical cool — without knowing why. The dramatist's hand is in the physics, not the ornament.
proposals.risk: Forty-five eras is forty-five arguments about what constitutes fidelity. The risk is that 'era-faithful' becomes a costume — surface markers (the Memphis squiggle, the Constructivist diagonal) without the underlying spatial logic that made those eras feel the way they felt. The counter is the light source discipline: if the motivated light is historically accurate and architecturally consistent across all layers, the costume becomes inhabited. The second risk is load time — three depth planes, a WebGL shader, and live text on mobile data. The counter is that the shader library is written once and cached; the plate is a single compressed image; the foreground cut-outs are lightweight PNGs. The drama is in the composition, not the file size. This risk is worth taking because a flat era-card — a Deco pattern tiled behind some Cormorant type — is a museum gift-shop postcard. I reject this for a specific reason that has nothing to do with taste: the guest opening this evite has not chosen to attend a design lecture. proposals.title: One Rule Per Era
proposals.idea: Each evite is governed by exactly one extractable structural law from its era — not its palette, not its ornament — so the era teaches itself through constraint rather than costume.
proposals.geometry: A single declared proportional or compositional rule drives every spatial decision per card: Bauhaus uses the 3:5:8 Fibonacci column split and nothing else; Constructivism uses a single diagonal axis at 63° from which all elements hang or flee; Art Deco uses a bilateral symmetry spine with one deliberate break; Memphis uses a 24px modular grid with mandatory misregistration of exactly 6px on one axis only; Ukiyo-e uses a horizon pushed to 78% of card height forcing compression above and void below; each rule is declared in code as a single exported constant so it is auditable, falsifiable, and cannot drift across the collection.
proposals.typography: One typeface family per era, chosen for structural not decorative fit — Bauhaus: Space Grotesk (OFL, geometric, rational); Constructivism: Oswald (OFL, condensed, poster-weight); Art Deco: Playfair Display (OFL, high-contrast, vertical stress); Memphis: Space Mono (OFL, fixed-pitch, anti-calligraphic); Ukiyo-e: Noto Serif JP (OFL, structural Japanese-Latin bridge); Harlem Renaissance: DM Serif Display (OFL, editorial authority); Afrofuturism: Exo 2 (OFL, technical without coldness); Vaporwave: Share Tech Mono (OFL, CRT-plausible). Scale set by one declared ratio per era, applied to every text node — no mixed hierarchies. Case and tracking derived from the era's own print conventions, not from a universal brand system.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs. Every art plate is a Magnific generative render directed to produce a composition that could pass as a primary-source artifact — not an illustration of the era but a document from it. Prompt strategy: one draft grid of 12 plates per era cluster (3–4 eras per prompt), each plate constrained to the era's structural law in its composition, not just its surface. Plates are used as the locked background layer. Foreground cut-outs are procedurally masked vector-adjacent shapes derived from the plate's own geometry — extracted by threshold, not hand-drawn. No representational figures unless they are abstract enough to carry no identity.
proposals.texture: Texture is structural, not decorative: Bauhaus gets no texture — the WebGL layer is set to zero grain, zero shimmer, proving the rule holds without material help; Constructivism gets a single linen-weave displacement map at 4% opacity simulating Soviet agitprop paper stock; Art Deco gets a foil layer constrained to the symmetry spine only — shimmer that respects the geometry; Memphis gets a halftone noise at 12lpi rendered as a WebGL shader, not an image; Ukiyo-e gets a washi-tooth grain shader at 2% opacity, enough to imply handmade paper without illustrating it; every texture has a declared opacity ceiling coded as a constant — if it cannot be justified by the era's production method, it does not appear.
proposals.motion: Tilt-driven depth planes move only along the axis the era's structural law already implies — Constructivism's diagonal, Art Deco's spine, Bauhaus's column grid — so motion reveals the same geometry that stillness already contains. Candle flicker shader applies only to eras with candlelit or lantern contexts (Ukiyo-e, Harlem Renaissance salon); flicker is constrained to a Perlin range of 0.4–1.6 Hz, physically plausible, falsifiable. No era gets particle effects unless particles are structurally load-bearing in that era's visual language. Reduced-motion mode: all depth planes freeze, all shaders drop to static, the structural law remains legible because it was never carried by motion alone.
proposals.productionMethod: Each era is a Tela document template built from a shared component schema: one exported structural-law constant, one generative art plate (Magnific, 8–16 per prompt batch), one procedurally masked foreground layer, one WebGL effects config keyed to the declared constant, one typeface token, one live-text layer. The structural-law constant is the single source of truth — grid columns, axis angle, symmetry break, modular unit — everything else is derived from it in code. Era palette is a secondary token, applied after structure, never before. Text fields (name, date, venue) are always live, never baked. The 45-era collection is organized into prompt batches of 3–4 structurally similar eras to maximize plate diversity per Magnific credit.
proposals.humanTrace: The structural law for each era is written by a human who has read primary sources — Moholy-Nagy's grid notebooks, El Lissitzky's Proun studies, the Rinpa school's ma intervals — and translated one principle into one falsifiable code constant. The editorial decision of which principle is load-bearing is the human act. Every other output is derived.
proposals.risk: This direction risks feeling academic — a design-history lecture dressed as an invitation. That risk is worth it because the brief explicitly calls for a museum-grade style lesson you can send, and the only way to avoid pastiche is to make the lesson structural rather than cosmetic. If the rule is real, the card teaches. If it is only palette, it is a costume.

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will argue that an era's emotional register cannot survive reduction to one structural rule — that Harlem Renaissance editorial needs the full layered density of Opportunity magazine's covers, not a single declared axis. I disagree: the density of those covers was itself produced by a structural logic, and if we cannot name that logic as one auditable constant, we are applying the er

disputes.objection: The registration offset is declared as the governing constraint, but it is not a governing constraint — it is a texture applied to a constraint that does not exist. Each era's grid is redesigned from scratch, which means there is no single measure from which the collection hangs; there is only a series of independent formal arguments that share a production metaphor. A collection where Memphis refuses to resolve and Constructivism bleeds to its own diagonal axis and Ukiyo-e obeys a scroll proportion has no counterpoint — it has seven soloists playing in separate rooms, and calling the misregistration a cantus firmus does not make it one when there is no common voice for it to govern.
disputes.concession: The decision to make each grid an argument about the era's production constraint — not merely its aesthetic surface — is exactly the kind of structural thinking I demand, and the letterpress wipe entrance timed at 280ms with ink-bloom following at 120ms is genuine temporal hierarchy, not decoration.

disputes.objection: Removing texture when you can't justify it by production method is still a decorator's move — you're just decorating with absence, and absence that's been that carefully curated is its own kind of polish. Bauhaus gets zero grain to 'prove the rule holds' — that's a performance of restraint, not restraint. The evidence of the human decision gets laundered out in the name of rigor, and what's left is a system that can't be argued with because there's nothing left to push against.
disputes.concession: The one falsifiable code constant per era is right — declaring the structural law as an auditable exported variable before any content exists is exactly the kind of prior commitment that makes the whole run answerable to something, the way a registration mark makes every sheet answerable to the firs

disputes.objection: One rule per era is not restraint — it is a category error dressed as philosophy: drama is not the enemy of constraint, but a single exported constant cannot carry the emotional weight of an era, and when you flatten Harlem Renaissance salon culture or Afrofuturist cosmology into an auditable code variable you have not distilled the era, you have taxidermied it — legible from the outside, hollow at the center, and incapable of the kind of feeling that makes a person stop scrolling. The structural law becomes a label pinned to the specimen rather than the heartbeat inside it; you have built a very elegant vitrine and called it a stage.
disputes.concession: The insistence that every texture have a declared opacity ceiling coded as a constant — justified by production method or absent entirely — is exactly right, and I will carry that discipline into my own direction without apology.

disputes.objection: The theatrical diorama metaphor multiplies elements — depth planes, foil shimmer, bokeh origin, candle-flicker, spring-overshoot, curtain-lift easing — each individually justified, collectively a budget of attention that no single guest can spend. Three acts of motion plus a continuous shader loop is not atmosphere; it is a room where every surface is talking. I will defend the 35° constraint all day precisely because it reduces governing rules to one; this system multiplies governing rules and calls the result coherence.
disputes.concession: The single motivated light source as first decision — before any prompt is written, before any element exists — is structurally correct: a constraint that precedes its outputs is load-bearing, not decorative, and that sequencing discipline is exactly right.

synthesis.direction: Each era is governed by one declared cantus firmus — a primary geometric measure (golden section, modular unit, diagonal angle, depth-plane ratio) written as an exported code constant before any prompt is written, from which palette, type scale, ornament grammar, and motion intervals derive without exception. Art plates are Magnific renders directed by era-specific prompt grammars naming colour space, light source, substrate, and one required structural feature; one draft grid of 8–16 plates per era cluster covers the full 45 at flat cost. Texture is shader-only and era-faithful — foil, newsprint tooth, washi grain, CRT scanline — each with a declared opacity ceiling justified by the era's production method or absent entirely. Motion sequence is fixed: field → skeleton → cut-outs → WebGL → live text, with tilt-response axis locked to the cantus firmus direction so movement reveals the same geometry stillness already contains.
synthesis.keepFromCounterpoint: The Rebellious Hand's letterpress wipe entrance — plate appearing as a pull from the gripper edge at 280ms with ink-bloom following at 120ms — survives as the load animation for eras with relief-print histories (Constructivism, Ukiyo-e, Harlem Renaissance), because it makes the production method the first thing the guest feels, not a detail they notice later.
synthesis.editorCut: The Radical Minimalist removed the Baroque Dramatist's three-act theatrical timing with spring-overshoot settle and continuous shader loops running in perpetuity. The concession from the Dramatist's own disagreement was used against it: a constraint that precedes its outputs is load-bearing; a continuous candle-flicker loop running after the guest has read the invitation is ambient noise, not structure. synthesis.openDecision: Should the cantus firmus for each era be visible as a drawn element — a hairline grid, a ruled diagonal, a dot-grid ghost — at reduced opacity in the final card, making the structural law legible to guests who look for it, or should it remain invisible infrastructure, present only in the proportions it governs?
synthesis.ariaSummary:
The team split on one real fault line: whether era fidelity lives in process evidence or structural law. The Rebellious Hand argued that misregistration, ink starvation, and plate wear are not texture — they are testimony that these eras cost something to make, and sanding them off produces a vibe, not a lesson. The Classical Mind answered that a rupture is only legible against a rule it breaks, and a collection where every era redesigns its own grid from scratch has seven soloists and no common voice. I took the Classical side, for a reason the Radical Minimalist forced into the open: if the structural law is not declared as an auditable constant before the first prompt is written, the collection is answerable to nothing, and 'era-faithful' becomes a costume you can adjust until it flatters.

The one thing I kept from the Rebellious Hand is the letterpress wipe entrance for relief-print eras. The team agreed — including the Minimalist — that when the plate arrives as a pull from the press rather than a dissolve from black, the production method is the first argument the guest encounters. That timing (280ms wipe, 120ms ink-bloom) is not decoration; it is the cantus firmus arriving before the content does.

The editor cut the Baroque Dramatist's continuous shader loops. Three acts of motion plus perpetual candle-flicker is a room where every surface is talking. The Dramatist's own concession — that a constraint preceding its outputs is load-bearing, not decorative — was the cut. Shaders idle after resolve unless the guest is actively tilting. The drama is in the first two seconds; after that, the structure holds without performance.

One decision belongs to you, and it is not a small one: should the cantus firmus be drawn — a ghost grid, a ruled diagonal, a dot-grid at low opacity — so design-literate guests can see the law the card obeys? Or does it stay invisible, present only in the proportions it produces? The first makes the lesson explicit and rewards attention. The second makes the lesson structural and rewards intuition. The council did not resolve this. You should.
